topic: Prepositions of Material (Made of vs. Made from)
said: Is it made out from plastic?
why: Use 'made of' when the material retains its physical identity without chemical transformation. Use 'made from' when it transforms (e.g., paper is made from wood).
spoken: Is it made out from plastic?
note: Use 'made of' when the material retains its physical identity without chemical transformation. Use 'made from' when it transforms (e.g. paper is made from wood).

said: The bus is green and large
why: In standard English adjective sequence, physical dimension and size always precede color: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color.
spoken: The bus is green and large
note: In standard English adjective sequence, physical dimension and size always precede color: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color.

said: My laptop was upset because doing too much things
natural: My laptop froze / crashed because it was handling too many background tasks simultaneously.
why: Personifying hardware as 'upset' is endearing, but 'froze / crashed' and 'too many tasks' (countable) represents polished professional English.
spoken: My laptop was upset because doing too much things
polished: My laptop froze / crashed because it was handling too many background tasks simultaneously.
note: Personifying hardware as 'upset' is endearing, but 'froze / crashed' and 'too many tasks' (countable) represents polished professional English.

said: The monkey driving the bus in the zoo
natural: The monkey was driving the bus through the zoo while the tourists ran away...
why: Anchor continuous background actions in past narratives with the past continuous (was/were + -ing) combined with a time conjunction (while / as).
spoken: The monkey driving the bus in the zoo
polished: The monkey was driving the bus through the zoo while the tourists ran away...
note: Anchor continuous background actions in past narratives with the past continuous (was/were + -ing) combined with a time conjunction (while / as).

said: The spaceship crashed because the speed
natural: The spaceship crashed due to extreme speed / because of its extreme speed
why: 'Because' introduces a full clause (subject + verb); 'due to' or 'because of' introduces a noun phrase ('its extreme speed').
spoken: The spaceship crashed because the speed
polished: The spaceship crashed due to extreme speed / because of its extreme speed
note: 'Because' introduces a full clause (subject + verb); 'due to' or 'because of' introduces a noun phrase ('its extreme speed').

natural: The words are difficult / The word module is challenging
why: Subject-verb agreement: 'words' is plural, requiring the plural verb 'are'.
polished: The words are difficult / The word module is challenging
note: Subject-verb agreement: 'words' is plural, requiring the plural verb 'are'.
